budget_policy.watchdog: per exact node ID, starts in pytest_runtest_protocol before fixture setup; same cleanup epoch covers owned process cleanup and all fixture finalizers via installed_controller
budget_policy.runtime_budget_reason: Private isolated Temporal server startup, registry/config manifests, SCRAM dispatcher/worker processes, direct history plus recovery and bounded shutdown occur within setup/body.
budget_policy.sql_budget_reason: The unadmitted non-create case uses only actual SCRAM claim_delivery SQL and no Temporal or runtime process; do not wait for a lease timeout.
budget_policy.execution_risk: All budgets include fixtures, but actual runner integration and fixture-finalizer duration remain unverified and must be proven before execution authorization.

evidence_privacy.public_summary: Only independently reviewed normalized synthetic case IDs, outcomes, counts and hashes; never credentials, private manifests, raw SQL/history/logs, or process identities.

cases.purpose: Current membership revocation wins when committed before the first worker projection.
cases.target: One real admitted create workflow and actual projector worker paused immediately before the first project_activation SQL call.
cases.method: Private child validates manifests, then subclasses the actual ExecutionStore to block before delegating the real SQL function. Operator independently deactivates the membership; API read must return 403; release the actual worker.
cases.pass_criteria: Exactly one rejected immutable receipt whose independently reconstructed proposal digest matches ifpmic.b03.transition.v1; error code FORBIDDEN, no QUEUED revision or business projection. The previously authorized run completes with result code FORBIDDEN; no workflow failure event.
cases.expected: 215s body/setup + 25s shared cleanup; current API authorization reflects revoked membership while the existing admitted run remains bound.
cases.evidence: Private before/revocation/after owner snapshots, API status, direct framed history and process journal with child PID/start-ticks; normalized reviewed summary only.
cases.recovery: Always release the barrier; stop only recorded owned process identities, verify absence, preserve failed evidence, and let fixture finalizers dispose the isolated workspace/database. Never edit the receipt.

cases.purpose: Current profile eligibility revocation wins when committed before the first worker projection.
cases.target: One real admitted create workflow paused immediately before its first actual project_activation SQL function call.
cases.method: Private child validates manifests, then test-only ExecutionStore subclass blocks before the real call. Operator inserts the real eligibility revocation; API read remains 200/DRAFT; release the worker.
cases.pass_criteria: Exactly one rejected immutable receipt whose independently reconstructed proposal digest matches ifpmic.b03.transition.v1; error code PROFILE_INELIGIBLE, DRAFT revision remains zero, no QUEUED projection, and the bound workflow completes with the same rejected result.
cases.expected: 215s body/setup + 25s shared cleanup; API access is independent from profile eligibility while projection rechecks that eligibility.
cases.evidence: Private literal SQL snapshots, API result, direct framed workflow history, PID/start-tick journal, source/environment pins and timing.
cases.recovery: Always release the barrier; stop and verify only owned processes; preserve evidence and use fixture finalizers. Do not rewrite receipts or history.

cases.purpose: A committed projection receipt remains authoritative after membership is revoked and the worker loses its activity result.
cases.target: Actual worker paused after the real project_activation transaction committed but before returning the Activity result.
cases.method: Observe one committed applied receipt and no matching ActivityTaskCompleted in direct history; revoke membership; SIGKILL the journaled PID only after start-tick identity check; start the normal worker on the same build/config/storage and await history completion.
cases.pass_criteria: Receipt and binding remain byte/value-identical, no duplicate revision/effect occurs, and the same run records one completed project_activation activity after recovery. No attempt-count assumption is made.
cases.expected: 215s body/setup + 25s shared cleanup including restart and history convergence; API membership revocation does not alter an immutable prior receipt.
cases.evidence: Owner snapshots before/after, direct history before kill/after replay, exact PID/start-tick kill journal and owned-process absence evidence.
cases.recovery: Release the private result barrier, stop only owned identities, verify absence and preserve the receipt/history evidence; never manufacture a retry or edit state.

cases.purpose: A committed projection receipt remains authoritative after eligibility is revoked and the worker loses its activity result.
cases.target: Actual projector paused after PostgreSQL commit and before its activity result reaches Temporal.
cases.method: Verify committed applied receipt and absent matching ActivityTaskCompleted; insert eligibility revocation, kill the saved worker PID after start-tick check, restart the normal worker on unchanged storage/build, and observe direct history.
cases.pass_criteria: Existing receipt/binding is unchanged and the same workflow run completes the activity once after recovery, with no duplicate business effect or revision.
cases.expected: 215s body/setup + 25s shared cleanup including real worker restart and history convergence.
cases.evidence: Private SQL snapshots, pre/post framed history, PID/start-tick lifecycle journal and source/environment hashes.
cases.recovery: Release barrier and stop/verify only owned identities. Preserve failed history and receipts without resetting state.

cases.purpose: A non-create command cannot be dispatched or consumed before a workflow binding is admitted.
cases.target: Synthetic accepted human-submission route/outbox in a real isolated fixture database, with no binding or workflow server.
cases.method: Owner seeds only the immutable command and outbox, calls actual claim_delivery through the SCRAM dispatcher role, then reads actual owner tables. The synthetic registered endpoint is never contacted.
cases.pass_criteria: claim_delivery returns idle; outbox remains pending at generation zero; no claim token, delivery attempt, binding, scope, receipt, revision, or human-task consumption appears.
cases.expected: 25s body/setup + 5s shared cleanup. SQL-only case must not wait for Temporal or an expiry interval.
cases.evidence: Private before/after owner snapshots and literal claim result, source/environment manifests and timing; no raw SQL publicly.
cases.recovery: No process is started. Preserve any failed snapshot and allow bounded fixture cleanup to dispose of the isolated DB/workspace.

cases.purpose: A durable non-create command signals the already admitted run without creating business state or a second workflow.
cases.target: Normally admitted and activated workflow plus one owner-seeded synthetic human-submission command/outbox, delivered by the actual dispatcher.
cases.method: Run actual dispatcher/worker and baseline create to completion; seed the non-create route/outbox; make it due; await real signal delivery attempt; compare owner SQL before/after and direct Temporal signal history plus workflow query.
cases.pass_criteria: Exactly one command_available signal reaches the existing run; accepted create provenance, binding, scope, receipt and revision remain unchanged; one workflow start and notification_count=1. No new run/activity/business effect or human task consumption. H4 endpoint/task acceptance remains pending.
cases.expected: 215s body/setup + 25s shared cleanup including real Temporal server and dispatcher/worker startup.
cases.evidence: Private SQL snapshots, signal payload/history and workflow query result, process PID/start-tick journal, source/environment pins and timing.
cases.recovery: Stop and verify only owned processes, preserve actual history and SQL evidence, and dispose through fixture cleanup. Never delete signal/history or reset the command.

cases.purpose: A real namespace retention lookup failure after actual history NotFound never authorizes workflow Start.
cases.target: Real dispatcher private child observes the isolated Temporal namespace before the owned Temporal server is stopped and retention RPC is attempted.
cases.method: Test-only TemporalTransport subclass records actual MissingHistory then waits. Parent confirms no run via actual list RPC, gracefully stops the owned server, releases child to call the unchanged super().retention_seconds() RPC, then queries owner SQL.
cases.pass_criteria: Actual describe_namespace RPC fails through production handling; binding/outbox/attempt quarantine RETENTION_UNVERIFIED; all start-window fields/run ID remain NULL, and no scope, receipt, job mutation or workflow Start exists.
cases.expected: 215s body/setup + 25s shared cleanup; real history NotFound and real subsequent retention RPC failure are causally ordered. No guessed retention/default is accepted.
cases.evidence: Private direct list/history observation, actual barrier events, literal owner snapshots, Temporal and dispatcher PID/start-tick stop records and exact pins.
cases.recovery: Always release the RPC barrier; stop only owned process identities and verify absence. Preserve evidence and run bounded fixture cleanup.

cases.purpose: An unsolicited successful Worker.run return is treated as runtime failure.
cases.target: Actual execution_runtime.main/run in a manifest-validated private child with a narrowly injected Worker subclass.
cases.method: After the real child connects to registered PG/Temporal dependencies, private barrier releases the injected Worker.run to return None; inspect process result and fixed stdout.
cases.pass_criteria: Child exits 3 with only DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE on stdout, no execution binding is created, and the exact child identity is absent.
cases.expected: 215s body/setup + 25s shared cleanup; injection is private constructor replacement only, not a product environment switch.
cases.evidence: Private event/log files, registration/owner snapshot, PID/start-tick lifecycle and exit status; source/environment pins.
cases.recovery: Release child barrier and stop/verify only owned processes; preserve failed logs privately and dispose fixtures.

cases.purpose: An unsolicited fatal Worker.run exception is surfaced as a runtime failure.
cases.target: Actual execution_runtime.main/run with a privately injected Worker whose run raises after a parent-controlled barrier.
cases.method: Child validates manifest/config and real registry before SDK dependency replacement; parent releases the fatal worker action and records the actual process outcome.
cases.pass_criteria: The exception yields exit 3 and fixed DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE output, no new binding, and child PID/start-tick is absent.
cases.expected: 215s body/setup + 25s shared cleanup; no SDK return is mocked and production runtime handles task failure.
cases.evidence: Private child event/logs, SQL no-binding oracle, lifecycle journal and exact source/environment hashes.
cases.recovery: Release barriers, stop only owned identities, verify absence, and preserve failed evidence.

cases.purpose: A fatal Worker task racing with SIGTERM is still surfaced instead of being swallowed as normal shutdown.
cases.target: Actual runtime child with a private Worker subclass that sends SIGTERM to its own saved process and raises a fatal exception in the same task turn.
cases.method: Wait for the child’s fatal-armed event, release the action, require the private event ordering (task action, self-SIGTERM, exception path), then inspect actual exit and fixed stdout.
cases.pass_criteria: Unrequested task failure exits 3, not normal exit 0; output is fixed DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE; no binding is created and owned process is absent.
cases.expected: 215s body/setup + 25s shared cleanup; exact asyncio signal/task scheduling remains an execution uncertainty until run on pinned versions.
cases.evidence: Private monotonic event records, process lifecycle/exit, SQL no-binding snapshot, source/environment/toolchain pins.
cases.recovery: Release any pending barrier and stop/verify only owned identities; preserve event order and logs.

cases.purpose: Requested SIGTERM remains a graceful shutdown control and does not become a false fatal-worker result.
cases.target: Actual execution_runtime child with registered worker and private Worker subclass waiting for runtime shutdown().
cases.method: Wait for Worker.run entry, signal only the saved child PID after validating start ticks, and observe worker shutdown and process exit.
cases.pass_criteria: Child exits 0 with no diagnostic stdout, and the journaled PID/start-tick is absent.
cases.expected: 215s body/setup + 25s shared cleanup; checks normal requested-stop path in contrast with the fatal cases.
cases.evidence: Private worker event, exact signal/PID/start-tick journal, stdout and exit status, source/environment hashes.
cases.recovery: Stop and verify only the owned child/services; preserve failed evidence and use fixture cleanup.

cases.purpose: An uncancellable real PostgreSQL driver thread cannot prevent bounded worker-process termination or commit partial projection state.
cases.target: Actual worker activity and project_activation transaction; injected DB connection wrapper executes the actual SQL function and then blocks on real SELECT pg_sleep(30) on the same open transaction.
cases.method: Observe private pg_sleep barrier and independent pg_stat_activity evidence for exact projector role/backend PID, active SELECT pg_sleep(30), and non-NULL xact_start, with DRAFT/no-receipt owner SQL state. SIGTERM the exact worker PID after start-tick check; wait for runtime self-exit within 15s+3s, then independently observe exact backend disappearance by pre-query event time+40s (capped by original body deadline); restart normal worker and inspect receipt/history recovery.
cases.pass_criteria: Worker exits 3 within 15s+3s and is absent; the exact observed PostgreSQL backend disappears and uncommitted function effects roll back (no receipt or revision), with no activity completion before recovery. Normal restart applies exactly one receipt/revision and one same-run activity completion.
cases.expected: 215s body/setup + 25s shared cleanup includes SIGTERM watchdog, PG rollback observation, real worker restart and history convergence; pinned DB driver/runtime behavior is an explicit runtime uncertainty.
cases.evidence: Private pg_sleep event, independent exact-role/backend/query/xact_start pg_stat_activity snapshots, owner SQL before/after kill/recovery, direct framed history, PID/start-tick journal and exact pins.
cases.recovery: Never signal an unowned process. Stop/verify only owned processes, preserve SQL/history evidence, and allow fixture finalizers to remove isolated resources.
